mainTopic: A gift of all a man's property to his wife: is it real ownership or just management, and when does such a gift cost her the כתובה?
overview: Earlier, the גמרא taught that when a שכיב מרע writes all his property to his wife, he only makes her an אפוטרופוס, so that people will respect her. רבא asks whether the same is true of a healthy man (בריא). The גמרא tries to answer from a ברייתא. There, a man gave his wife all his property and then an earlier שטר חוב appeared. The חכמים rule that she loses both her כתובה and the gift. The proof is that, without the creditor, the gift would have been hers, so the ברייתא seems to be about a healthy man. The proof is pushed off: the ברייתא can be about a שכיב מרע in cases where the wife really does acquire. רב נחמן then rules like the חכמים. The גמרא asks whether he ignores אומדנא, since he follows רבי שמעון בן מנסיא elsewhere. It answers that a wife wants it known that she was given everything. Finally, the גמרא quotes a משנה: a wife who is written a bit of land while the sons get the property loses her כתובה. רב, שמואל, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא each explain what case that means.

steps.title: Does a healthy man also just appoint his wife as manager?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether the rule for a שכיב מרע (writing all his property to his wife only makes her an אפוטרופא) also applies to a healthy man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: What about a healthy man? Maybe only a dying man wants his wife to be respected and listened to after he dies, so he makes her manager. A healthy man is still around himself, so maybe he really meant to give her the property. Or maybe a healthy man also wants her to be respected starting right now?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a question (בעיא). He wants to know if a healthy man who writes all his property to his wife is also only making her a manager, the way a dying man is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two sides. Side one: a dying man needs his wife to have authority after he is gone, but a healthy man is still standing there and can protect her honor himself, so his document must be a real gift. Side two: even a healthy man may want people to listen to her from now on, so it is still just an appointment as manager.

keyTerms.meaning: He asks a question / raises an open problem (a בעיא)
A person who is dangerously ill, on his deathbed
It is pleasing to him / he prefers
That her word be listened to (that she gets respect and authority)
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of the question)

phrases.english: Rava asked:
In the case of a healthy person, what is the law?
Is it only a person on his deathbed who prefers
that her word be listened to,
but a healthy person is still standing here himself?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא בָּרִיא נָמֵי נִיחָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Or perhaps a healthy person also prefers
that her word be listened to starting from now?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the earlier rule about a שכיב מרע to the case of a healthy man.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a healthy man who writes all his property to his wife also make her only an אפוטרופא, or does he give her a real gift?

steps.title: A ברייתא: gift of produce or of part of the property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא. If a man gives his wife the produce of his property, or a fraction of it, she still collects her כתובה from the land or from what is left.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If a man writes the produce of his property to his wife, she collects her כתובה from the land itself. If he writes her half, a third, or a quarter of his property, she collects her כתובה from the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: With 'תא שמע,' the גמרא starts bringing a ברייתא to try to answer רבא. These first lines set up the cases; the important part for the proof is coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting a partial gift does not cost her the כתובה. She keeps the gift and still collects the כתובה from whatever he did not give her. This sets up the contrast with the next case, where he gives her everything.

keyTerms.meaning: The produce or profits of his property
The rest (the property not given as a gift)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who writes the produce of his property to his wife:
she collects her marriage contract from the land itself.
If he gave her a half, a third, or a quarter of his property:
she collects her marriage contract from the rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a ברייתא as an attempt to answer רבא's question.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's question about a healthy man
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a man who gives gifts to his wife

steps.title: All the property was given, then a debt appears
steps.stepSummary: A man gave all his property to his wife, and then an earlier שטר חוב turned up. רבי אליעזר says she tears up the gift and relies on her כתובה. The חכמים say she tears up the כתובה and relies on the gift, so she ends up with nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote all his property to his wife, and then a loan document came out against him: רבי אליעזר says her gift is torn up and she relies on her כתובה. The חכמים say her כתובה is torn up and she relies on her gift, and she ends up bald on both sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a מחלוקת. It is about a man who gave his wife all his property and was later found to owe money from an earlier loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר lets her drop the gift and collect with her כתובה, which is older than the loan, so the creditor cannot take the property from her. The חכמים say that by accepting a gift of everything, she gave up her כתובה. Her gift is newer than the loan, so the creditor takes it, and she is left with neither.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be torn up (it loses its force)
And let her rely on / remain with
Bald from here and from there (left with nothing either way)

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים do not mean she keeps the property through her gift. Relying on the gift means giving up the כתובה. The creditor then takes the gift, because his loan came first.

phrases.english: If he wrote all his property to his wife,
and a loan document came out against him:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
Let her gift be torn up, and let her rely on her marriage contract.
And the Sages say:
Let her marriage contract be torn up, and let her rely on her gift;
and she is found bald from here and from there.
phrases.notes: "Bald" here means left with nothing: the creditor takes the gift, and the כתובה is gone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the case of a gift of all his property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: she drops the gift and collects with her כתובה. חכמים: by taking the gift she loses her כתובה, and the earlier creditor takes the gift, so she ends up with nothing.

steps.title: A real case: the חכמים ruled she gets nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה הנחתום tells of a real case involving his niece, who was also his daughter-in-law. The חכמים ruled that her כתובה is torn up and she ends up with nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה the baker said: This exact thing happened to my sister's daughter, who is my daughter-in-law. The case came before the חכמים, and they said: Her כתובה is torn up and she relies on her gift, and she ends up bald on both sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a story that backs up the חכמים' view. The גמרא has now laid out the full source it will use to answer רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that the חכמים' ruling was actually applied in a real court case, not only stated in theory. In the next step, the גמרא builds its proof on the flip side of this case: she loses the gift only because a שטר חוב appeared, so without one she would own the property.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, backed by a real court case, a wife who accepts a gift of all her husband's property loses her כתובה. For רבא's question, the key point is different: the ברייתא assumes the gift is truly hers unless a creditor shows up.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda the baker said:
There was an incident, and the matter happened
to my sister's daughter, my daughter-in-law,
phrases.notes: She was his niece, and she was also married to his son.

phrases.english: and the case came before the Sages,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרוּ: תִּקָּרַע כְּתוּבָּתָהּ וְתַעֲמוֹד עַל מַתְּנָתָהּ,
phrases.english: and they said: Let her marriage contract be torn up, and let her rely on her gift,
and she is found bald from here and from there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the חכמים' position from step 3 with a real case.
steps.raayaObject: The חכמים' ruling that she loses her כתובה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real case brought before the חכמים, reported by רבי יהודה הנחתום

steps.title: Inferring from the ברייתא that a healthy man's gift works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reasons that she loses the gift only because a creditor showed up, so without one she owns it. That cannot be a שכיב מרע, who only makes her an אפוטרופוס, so the ברייתא must mean a healthy man.
steps.simpleTranslation: The only reason she loses is that a debt document turned up against him. If no debt document turned up, she would own the property. Which man are we talking about? If he was dying, you already said he only made her a steward! So isn't it a healthy man?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the proof it started in Step 2, using the ברייתא to answer רבא's question about a healthy man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumes the gift really belongs to her unless a שטר חוב interferes. A gift from a שכיב מרע would only make her a manager, not an owner. So the case seems to be a בריא, which would mean a healthy man's gift to his wife takes full effect.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason (often used to infer the opposite case)
Rather, isn't it…? (introduces the proposed conclusion)

phrases.english: The reason is that a promissory note came out against him,

phrases.aramaic: הָא לֹא יָצָא עָלָיו שְׁטַר חוֹב – קָנְיָא.
phrases.english: but if no promissory note came out against him, she acquires.
And in what case is this?
If you say it is about a person on his deathbed,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמְרַתְּ לֹא עֲשָׂאָהּ אֶלָּא אַפּוֹטְרוֹפּוֹס!
phrases.english: but you said he only made her a steward!
phrases.notes: This points back to the rule in רבא's question in Step 1.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not about a healthy man?

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּיָצָא עָלָיו שְׁטַר חוֹב, הָא לֹא יָצָא עָלָיו שְׁטַר חוֹב – קָנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא quoted in Steps 2–4 to answer the question of Step 1.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's question: does a healthy man who writes all his property to his wife give her real ownership?
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא assumes the gift belongs to her when no creditor appears, which does not fit a שכיב מרע.

steps.title: The ברייתא can still be about a dying man
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The ברייתא can be about a שכיב מרע, in the special cases where he does give real ownership: all those cases according to רב עוירא, or a betrothed or divorced wife according to רבינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is about a dying man. רב עוירא places the ברייתא in all of those cases, and רבינא places it in the case of a man's betrothed wife or his divorced wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The ברייתא does not have to be talking about a healthy man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that she is only an אפוטרופוס does not cover every case. There are cases where even a שכיב מרע's gift gives her full ownership, and the ברייתא can be set in those cases. So רבא's question about a בריא stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (keeps the original reading and rejects the proof)
He sets it in (explains which case the source is about)
A betrothed woman (after קידושין, before נישואין)

phrases.english: Actually, it is about a person on his deathbed;
and Rav Avira sets it in all of them,
phrases.notes: He means all the cases discussed earlier where, in רב עוירא's view, she really gets the property.

phrases.english: Ravina sets it
in the case of his betrothed wife or his divorced wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of Step 5 by placing the ברייתא in a different case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide רבא's question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed every שכיב מרע's gift only makes her an אפוטרופוס. In fact some cases (all of them for רב עוירא, ארוסה and גרושה for רבינא) give her full ownership.
steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to answer רבא from the ברייתא fails. The ברייתא can describe a שכיב מרע in the cases where the wife really does acquire.

steps.title: רב נחמן rules like the חכמים: she loses everything
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר מניומי reports that רב נחמן ruled like the חכמים in the ברייתא. Her כתובה is torn up, she is left with the gift, and the creditor takes that, so she has nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: the הלכה is that her כתובה is torn up and she relies on her gift, so she ends up bald on both sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a final ruling on the argument between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים from Step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking the gift counts as giving up her כתובה. Once the earlier creditor collects the property, the gift is gone too. So she has neither her כתובה nor her gift.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be torn up (the document is cancelled)
Bald on both sides: left with nothing either way

phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Minyumi said
that Rav Nachman said: The halakha is:
her marriage contract is torn up and she relies on her gift,
and she is found bald from here and from there.
phrases.notes: A picture of losing on both sides: the כתובה is gone and the creditor takes the gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבא discussion and gives the practical ruling on the dispute quoted in Step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows the חכמים: accepting the gift cancels her כתובה, so when the earlier creditor collects, she is left with nothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling for a wife who accepts all her husband's property as a gift. The next step challenges it.

steps.title: Does רב נחמן ignore what she really intended?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised: does this mean רב נחמן does not follow אומדנא, judging by what a person obviously intended?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that רב נחמן does not go after assessing a person's intention?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge against רב נחמן's ruling. This step sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No wife would knowingly accept a gift that could leave her with nothing. If the court judges by her obvious intention, she should not lose her כתובה. So רב נחמן's ruling seems to ignore אומדנא, which the גמרא is surprised to hear.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say…? (introduces a surprised challenge)
An assessment of what a person clearly intended, even if he did not say it

phrases.english: Is that to say that Rav Nachman does not go
after assessment of intention?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּלָא אָזֵיל רַב נַחְמָן בָּתַר אוּמְדָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of רב נחמן in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the wife loses both her כתובה and her gift.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Judging by her obvious intention (אומדנא), she never meant to give up her כתובה and risk getting nothing. Ruling that she loses everything seems to go against that principle.

steps.title: A ברייתא Showing רב נחמן Does Follow Obvious Intent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a father who gave away everything after hearing his son had died. רב נחמן rules like רבי שמעון בן מנסיא that the gift is cancelled, which means he does follow אומדנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: A man's son went overseas, and the father heard that his son had died. So he wrote all his property over to other people, and afterward the son came back. The gift stands. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says: The gift does not stand, because if he had known his son was alive, he would not have written it. And רב נחמן said: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up its surprise from Step 8. It brings a case where רב נחמן clearly judges by what the person obviously meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא cancels the gift only because of what the father would obviously have wanted. That is אומדנא, and רב נחמן rules like him. So it is hard to understand why רב נחמן, in Step 7, did not use אומדנא to protect the wife's כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: His gift is a valid gift
The final ruling follows this opinion

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָלַךְ בְּנוֹ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם,
phrases.english: But isn't it taught: If one's son went overseas,
and he heard that his son died,
and he went and wrote all his property to others,
and afterward his son came back –
his gift is a valid gift.
Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:
His gift is not a valid gift –
for had he known that his son was alive,
he would not have written them over.
And Rav Nachman said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the surprise in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling in Step 7 that the wife ends up with nothing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן rules like רבי שמעון בן מנסיא, so he does follow אומדנא. Then he should also use it to assume the wife never meant to give up her כתובה.

steps.title: The Wife Wants It Known She Was Given Everything
steps.stepSummary: The wife's case is different. She is happy for people to hear that her husband wrote all his property to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because she is pleased that word goes out about her that he wrote all that property to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רב נחמן does follow אומדנא, but here the obvious guess actually goes the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the father, the obvious guess is that he never meant to cut off his son. With the wife, there is a real reason she would accept this gift even at a cost: the honor of being known as the one he trusted with everything. So we cannot assume she did not mean to give up her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: She is pleased; it suits her
A voice; public word or reputation

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן does follow אומדנא. In the wife's case, the obvious guess is that she wanted the honor of the gift, so her כתובה is still lost.

phrases.english: It is different there,
for she is pleased that word goes out about her
that he wrote those properties over to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 8 and 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רב נחמן follows אומדנא, he should assume the wife never meant to give up her כתובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Here the obvious guess is that she wants the public honor, so she knowingly accepts the risk.

steps.title: A משנה: Land to the Wife Costs Her the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: A new related source is quoted. If a man writes his property to his sons and writes any amount of land to his wife, she loses her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: One who writes his property to his sons, and writes his wife any amount of land, she has lost her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה from somewhere else. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier cases, this is about a wife losing her כתובה because of how her husband handed out his property. Here she gets only a small piece of land, and the sons get the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
Any amount of land, even a tiny piece

phrases.english: We learned there: One who writes his property to his sons,
and wrote his wife any amount of land –
she has lost her ketubah.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife who is written any land while the sons get the property loses her כתובה.

steps.title: Why Would a Small Gift Erase Her כתובה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is puzzled. Why should getting a small piece of land make her lose her whole כתובה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Just because he wrote her any amount of land, she has lost her כתובה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule as strange. It is asking what exact case the משנה must be talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting a gift should only help her. It does not seem to show that she agreed to give up her כתובה, so the משנה needs to be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: He wrote over to her (gave her in writing)

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּכָתַב לָהּ קַרְקַע כׇּל שֶׁהוּא –
phrases.english: Because he wrote her any amount of land –
she has lost her ketubah?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּכָתַב לָהּ קַרְקַע כׇּל שֶׁהוּא
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that she loses her כתובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A gift to her does not show she gave up her rights, so why should she lose them?

steps.title: רב: She Helped Transfer the Property to the Sons
steps.stepSummary: רב says the משנה is about a husband who gives the sons ownership through her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The case is where he gives them ownership through her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers by narrowing the משנה to a specific case. The wife herself takes part in handing the property to the sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she helps give the property to the sons, she clearly agrees they should have it. That is why she loses her claim on it for her כתובה.

phrases.english: Rav said:
It is where he grants them ownership through her.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the sons. She is the one who takes hold of the property for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A small gift alone makes her lose the כתובה, which makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: She took part in giving the sons ownership, so she clearly agreed.

steps.title: שמואל: She Watched in Silence
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says it is enough that the husband divided the property in front of her and she said nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: The case is where he divides the property in front of her and she stays silent.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different, broader answer. She does not need to take part; staying quiet while he divides it is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל treats her silence as agreement. If she cared about her כתובה, she should have spoken up while the property was being handed out.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
It is where he divides it in front of her and she is silent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer, wider than רב's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to a specific case
steps.terutzMaskana: Her silence while he divides the property shows she agreed.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: He Gave Her the Land as Her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says the משנה is about a husband who told her to take this land for her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: The case is where he says to her: "Take this land for your כתובה."
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer. The land was given to her as payment for her כתובה, not as an extra gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she accepts this land as her כתובה, she has no more claim on the rest of the property. That is what the משנה means by "she lost her כתובה."
steps.whatToRemember: Three ways to explain the משנה: she helped transfer the property (רב), she watched in silence (שמואל), or the land was given as her כתובה (רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, said:
It is where he says to her: "Take this land for your ketubah."

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to a specific case
steps.terutzMaskana: The land was given and accepted as her כתובה, so she can claim nothing more.
